title: Perfectness criterion on a ringed site
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, small relative to the universe of its module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], and let $K\in D(\mathcal O)$. Use unbounded derived categories of sheaves of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A strictly perfect complex is a bounded complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free structure modules. On a ringed site, an object $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent if locally on every object of the site there are a strictly perfect complex $P^\bullet$ and a map $P^\bullet\to K$ in the derived category inducing isomorphisms on $H^j$ for $j>m$ and a surjection on $H^m$; it is pseudo-coherent if this holds for every integer $m$. Write $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$ for the derived tensor product, computed by a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex] and the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. An object $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, for integers $a\le b$, if $H^j(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)=0$ for every structure-module sheaf $F$ and every $j\notin[a,b]$. It has finite Tor dimension if such an interval exists; it locally has finite Tor dimension if locally on every site object some such interval exists, allowed to depend on the covering member. Then $K$ is perfect, meaning locally on every site object isomorphic in the derived category to a strictly perfect complex, if and only if $K$ is pseudo-coherent and locally has finite Tor dimension. No quasi-compactness, coherence of $\mathcal O$, or global boundedness of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Suppose $K$ is perfect. For each site object choose a cover on which $K$ is isomorphic to a bounded complex $P$ of finite-free summands. The same isomorphism is an $m$-pseudo-coherent approximation for every $m$, so the definition gives pseudo-coherence. Each term is flat: after tensoring an exact sequence, its tensor sequence is a retract of the exact sequence obtained by taking a finite direct sum of that sequence, hence is exact. Here tensor is additive and its unit is the structure sheaf. Choose any interval containing the finitely many nonzero degrees of $P$ (choose $[0,0]$ for the zero complex). The bounded-flat-model equivalence gives the Tor bound for $K$ on this covering member, as required.

Conversely fix an object $U$. Choose a cover on which $K$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, allowing a different interval on each member. Work on one such localized site. Pseudo-coherence restricts: apply its covering condition to each object over $U$; exact restriction preserves the cohomology comparisons, and relocalization identifies the resulting slices with the original slices. Choose an $(a-1)$-approximation $P_0\to K$ by a strictly perfect complex. Replace $P_0$ by its brutal truncation $P=\sigma_{\ge a-1}P_0$ and compose the inclusion with this map. The new complex is still bounded with finite-free-summand terms and its comparison is an isomorphism on $H^j$ for every $j\ge a$: kernels and incoming images in those degrees have not changed. Its terms are flat by the retract argument of Step 1. The Tor interval persists under any further localization by the cited restriction lemma.

source.place: Tag 08G8 (lemma-perfect), implication (2) to (1); Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), first paragraph.

proof.text: Put $Q=\operatorname{coker}(P^{a-1}\to P^a)$. The flat-approximation-opcycle lemma applies on this localized site: $P$ is bounded flat, zero below $a-1$, its comparison is an isomorphism in every degree at least $a$, and $K$ has the required universal Tor interval. Thus $Q$ is flat. It is also finitely presented. Indeed choose splittings $P^{a-1}\xrightarrow{i_1}\mathcal O^r\xrightarrow{p_1}P^{a-1}$ and $P^a\xrightarrow{i_0}\mathcal O^s\xrightarrow{p_0}P^a$. With $e=i_0p_0$, the map $\mathcal O^{r+s}\to\mathcal O^s$, $(x,y)\mapsto i_0d^{a-1}p_1(x)+(1-e)y$, has cokernel $Q$: its second summand kills the complement of $P^a$, and its first kills exactly the image of $d^{a-1}$. This gives a finite presentation, also after restriction to every slice.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), flatness of E′ and the finite-presentation hypothesis preceding application of Modules on Sites Tag 08FD.

proof.text: Form the good lower truncation $T=\tau_{\ge a}P$: its degree-$a$ term is $Q$, its higher terms are those of $P$, and its lower terms are zero. For the standard t-structure this is the lower truncation of $P$. The Tor assumption, tested on $\mathcal O$, gives $K\in D^{\ge a}$. By the left-adjoint property of lower truncation, the comparison $P\to K$ factors through $T\to K$. For $j\ge a$, the projection $P\to T$ induces the identity on cohomology, so this factor induces $H^j(P)\cong H^j(K)$; below $a$ both objects have zero cohomology. Both objects are bounded below, so the cited cohomology criterion makes $T\to K$ an isomorphism in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), lower truncation implicit in the final displayed complex. Standard good truncation and its adjunction identify its derived object.

proof.text: Apply the flat, locally finitely presented sheaf lemma to $Q$, whose two hypotheses were proved in Step 3. On a further cover $Q$ is a direct summand of a finite free structure module. Restrict $T$ to that cover. Exact restriction preserves the cokernel description and the derived isomorphism of Step 4. All its other terms retain their finite-free splittings. Hence this restricted bounded complex is strictly perfect and represents the restriction of $K$. Do not brutally cut off the high terms at $b$: their existing finite upper bound suffices. Compose the covers chosen for the local Tor bound, the pseudo-coherent approximation and the splitting of $Q$. Relocalization identifies every final representative with a representative on the corresponding original slice. Since $U$ was arbitrary this is exactly perfectness.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q95-cb9167c82 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 08G7 and 08G8 in sites-cohomology.tex in full. The item statement is unchanged and matches 08G8 on an arbitrary ringed site: 08FT pseudo-coherence for every m, the 08FZ Tor amplitude with a local interval that may vary by covering member, and 08G5 perfectness. There is no repair note and live/side-live still have the item unsplit, so the delivery is neither a re-split nor superseded. It cites no SGA source. Step 1: an isomorphism to a strictly perfect complex is an m-approximation for every m; summands of O^n are flat by additivity and unit (lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed), and lem-sp-ringed-site-tor-flat-model (2)=>(1) gives the Tor bound. Step 2: relocalization and exact restriction carry pseudo-coherence, lem-sf-site-tor-interval-restriction carries the Tor interval, and the brutal truncation at a-1 is a subcomplex that keeps H^j for j>=a. Step 3: every hypothesis of the new node holds. I checked that the map (x,y) -> i0 d p1 x + (1-e)y has cokernel exactly Q, which gives a global finite presentation. Step 4: the good truncation T is quasi-isomorphic to P/tau<=a-1 P, K lies in D>=a by the Tor test on O, the factorization uses the left adjoint of clause (1) of the heart lemma, and DerivedCategory.Plus.isIso_iff applies because T is bounded and K is in D>=a. Step 5: lem-sf-site-flat-fp-finite-retract gives local finite-free retracts of Q, so the restricted T is strictly perfect and the covers compose. New node lem-sfb-flat-approximation-opcycle is true by the 08G7 cone argument: C is R[2-a] with R = ker d^(a-1), tensoring with N makes S⊗N -> P^a⊗N injective, so Tor_1(Q,N) = 0 and Q is flat by 08FG. I tested it on P=O with K=0, and on [O -x-> O] over k[x] and [Z -2-> Z] over Z, which the Tor hypothesis excludes as it should. It is self-contained, statement-only, records all three search kinds, and is not a clause of the item. Duplicate search: opcycles-retract assumes an isomorphism, site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses is a smaller ingredient, the lem-pc-* 08CQ nodes are scheme-only and the remaining perfect-criterion nodes are ring-level. I accept the seven declared tool uses as generic. Advisory only: the unchanged item statement says locally without citing the localization or derived-restriction definitions in stmt_deps.
